subject: FinTechCo — post-call recap, MAP & internal align before recontact
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Subject: FinTechCo — Post-call recap & mutual action plan

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

TL;DR
- Redwood can support FinTechCo's fraud-detection scoring pipeline with low-latency scoring at your expected QPS.
- Next step: technical deep-dive + mutual action plan (MAP) to align stakeholders and timing.

Notes from the call:
- Primary use case: real-time fraud scoring for checkout (sub-100ms in prod target)
- Initial scope: 2 dedicated nodes, batch re-scoring for historical retraining, embeddings for feature augmentation
- Success metrics: latency under 120ms p95, cost <$0.002/token, ability to pin model version for audit

Proposed MAP (attached):
1) Week 1: Technical deep dive (solutions engineer + infra) — scope, data flows, SLA needs
2) Week 2: PoC plan (sample data, metrics, runbook)
3) Week 3-6: PoC execution + weekly check-ins
4) Commercials: draft SOW and anticipated pricing for Dedicated deployment

Ask from you: please confirm stakeholders (procurement/legal contact) and whether the proposed timeline looks realistic. I attached the MAP and a one-pager for your review.

If it helps, Marcus (cc'd) can run a quick 30–45 minute technical session early next week to validate integration points.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding the thread (see below). Oliver hasn't replied to the MAP or my bump from yesterday. I want to align quickly on approach before I follow up again so we don't appear pushy and we bring the right value.

Proposed options (ranked):
1) Technical office hours (45m): Marcus leads a targeted session for their engineers — low lift, high signal.
2) Exec intro + ROI note: short note from Rachel to FinTech execs highlighting SLA & cost economics; could speed procurement.
3) Offer an initial, timeboxed PoC scope & SOW ask to procurement — clearer commercial ask but requires pricing approval.

My recommended next step: try option 1 (technical office hours) this week and simultaneously prepare a concise ROI one-pager we can share if procurement asks for numbers. If we still don't hear back after that, escalate to option 2.

Specific asks:
- Marcus: can you do a 45-min deep-dive this week (I can suggest Wed/Thu). Also please prepare a short list of integration risks and an initial PoC checklist.
- Laura: any CS/ops considerations you want mentioned in the session or shared in the MAP?
- Aditya/Rachel: if we need to surface pricing / discounts for an early win, what approval gate do we need?

I want to recontact Oliver on Monday 5/17 if we don't get a response — but I won't until we have Marcus lined up and a one-pager ready.

Thoughts?

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — happy to take the session. Wed (5/19) 10:00–10:45 PT or Thu (5/20) 14:00–14:45 PT both work on my side.

For the session I will:
- Prepare a 20–25 minute walkthrough of integration touch points (latency-critical paths, data requirements, auth)
- Bring a short PoC checklist (sample dataset, success metrics, runbook)
- Flag likely engineering blockers and mitigations (sandboxing, KV cache priming, telemetry hooks)

If we want to nudge procurement, I can include a slide with initial pricing bands but would prefer Rachel to handle any discount conversations.

I'll drop a short slide pack in the shared drive and can circulate it to Oliver directly if you want.
